prerequisites: Basic level of differential and integral calculus is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that starts from the base of general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities and solving exercises proposed in practical classes
Written exam on theoretical and operational concepts
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises and solving problem sets

assessment_rules: The written exam consists of solving theoretical-practical problems. Computer practices are evaluated via an exercise-solving test using statistical software, which may be a global practice in the last practical class. For the ordinary call, there will be no practical exam, and notes from practices and continuous evaluation will be maintained for the extraordinary call. Students may opt to retake the practical exam in the extraordinary call, waiving their previous practical grade. A student is considered 'NOT PRESENTED' if they do not attend the official exam, regardless of other evaluation parts.
